attempts.summary: Configured VLAN access-port segmentation on node1 (SONiC) separating node2's segment (eth1, VLAN 101) from node3's segment (eth2, VLAN 102) using the kernel-level vlan-aware "Bridge" device already present on SONiC-VS, since the Ethernet* SAI port abstraction is unbound from the real virtio NICs. eth1 and eth2 are untagged/PVID access ports in VLAN 101 and 102 respectively; node1 holds an SVI (Bridge.101 = 192.168.101.1/24, Bridge.102 = 192.168.102.1/24) giving it a working L3 link into each VLAN, while node2 (192.168.101.2/24 on enp8s0) and node3 (192.168.102.2/24 on enp8s0) cannot reach each other (different subnets, no cross-VLAN forwarding, ip_forward disabled on node1). Physical topology was first identified experimentally (eth1<->node2, eth2<->node3) via temporary IP/ping tests. Node2/node3 IP configs were made persistent via NetworkManager connection profiles (autoconnect) after discovering NM was clobbering ad hoc `ip addr` assignments on enp8s0. Node1's VLAN/bridge state was made persistent via a new enabled systemd oneshot unit (vlan-access-segmentation.service) that reapplies the configuration at boot, since raw `ip`/`bridge` state on SONiC-VS does not survive reboot and the Ethernet* configdb path isn't usable for these NICs. Ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy-state evidence, restarted each node individually (node1 via `reboot`, node2/node3 via `systemctl reboot`), confirmed changed boot_id and full recovery (VLAN config, IP config, and connectivity/isolation all confirmed intact) before moving to the next node. A benign duplicate-ICMP-reply artifact (0% packet loss, cosmetic DUP! in ping output) was observed and investigated; it is caused by the underlying nested-virtualization dataplane, not the VLAN configuration, and does not affect isolation or link correctness.
